g.text: CAP Theorem — what CP vs AP actually do during a network partition
Same setup both sides: two nodes replicating a value, network between them severs. The client on each side keeps writing.
Node A blocks/rejects the write — it cannot confirm B
has acknowledged, so it refuses rather than risk two
nodes disagreeing on the value of x.
Chooses Consistency over Availability: correctness of every
read is preserved, at the cost of the write not going through
Partition heals: conflict detected (x=5 vs x=9) —
resolved by last-write-wins or a vector-clock merge
Chooses Availability over Consistency: both writes
succeed immediately, but the two nodes briefly
disagree until the merge step above resolves it.
